scope: Fixed-scanner 2x2 source factorial plus same-SHA g1h1 repeat. Synthetic source metadata/size fixture with two roots, four warmed QuickJS runtimes. 60 s baseline, 240 s mixed pressure, 300 s natural cooldown per case; then separate diagnostic interventions. Includes expected 503 responses; zero errors means zero unexpected validation/transport failures. No actual business dependency or traffic replay. Linux amd64 only.

factor_definition.G: Added vhttpd idle-only process-wide GC coordinator and request activity hooks; normal Boehm GC remains enabled in G0 and G1. Existing legacy libc maintenance remains. This factor does not switch the collector/compiler version.
factor_definition.H: Five-file HTTP observation bundle: fixed bucket arrays, bounded history rings, deferred disabled-level JSON logging and snapshot conversion.

isolated_g0_pair_cold_residency_differen.scope: One sample each; measured mapping attribution, not a population-level causal estimate. Helper loading perturbs absolute memory.

confirmed: Large anonymous-residency differences are primarily GC object-heap pages, not a similarly enlarged conservatively marked object set. Full-GC marked bytes remain around 5.4-5.5 MiB.

Full collection makes additional whole blocks reusable without immediately reducing RSS. Explicit unmap reduces physical GC residency; libc trim has little or no extra effect in this fixture. See per-run values.
Read-only free-block ages in G1H0 and same-SHA G1H1 repeat show mapped resident free pages below the configured 7-collection unmap age. Age is collection epochs, not seconds.

G1 automatically reclaims after a 30-second quiet window, then background scanner allocation refills between the 16 MiB minimum heap / 8 MiB growth / 60-second cooldown safeguards. It does not control pressure-phase pool high water.
No idle coordinator collection attempt increased during sustained pressure or the held-request guard.

The same G1H1 binary has materially different pressure physical residency across repeats, so single-cell differences cannot identify one HTTP sub-edit as the unique cause. Mapped capacity is not physical residency.
inference: Most of the observed larger footprint is reclaimable GC pool/pending sweep state and block occupancy, rather than evidence of new unbounded application objects. Conservatively marked reachability is not exact business liveness.

After forced GC/unmap, GC pages remain assigned to object blocks while only a few KiB or less are whole free blocks; aggregate resident-minus-marked slack is consistent with partially occupied size-class blocks and collector caches. Exact slot ownership/false roots is not established.
unresolved: Pressure-phase high-water improvements and precise contribution of each HTTP sub-edit require further controlled allocation/occupancy profiling; same-SHA variation prevents a unique source-line attribution from this factorial.
No full 24-hour candidate acceptance, Windows coverage or real business replacement is provided by these short synthetic runs. P0-02 remains blocked.
measurement_limits: Natural phases exclude all debugger/helper/forced collection/trim interventions. Post-cooldown interventions are not natural acceptance data.

Marked histogram/region iteration is under GC allocation lock. Some scalar counters are read after unlock; the initial G0H1 FREE scalar drifted 16 KiB and is not used in preference to locked region bytes.
Forwarding callbacks overlap already-reported spans and are not additive allocated bytes. Use unique GC-section pagemap counts for physical residency.
Snapshots of external process metadata/pagemap/smaps are concurrent; epoch/header consistency checks reduce but do not eliminate races.
Minimal keeper calibration validates known 8 MiB reachability and unmapping; it did not exercise forwarding spans.
GC non-GC-byte accounting can unsigned-underflow; that raw counter is not an application live-byte count.
